title: Reducing and Oxidising Aldehydes and Ketones
subject: Chemistry
objective: Reduction is easy for both aldehydes and ketones, but in oxidation the aldehyde reacts at once and the ketone resists. The reason is one H atom.

fill.q: NaBH₄ reduces an aldehyde to a ____ alcohol.
NaBH₄ reduces a ketone to a ____ alcohol.
Clemmensen reduction uses zinc amalgam and concentrated ____.
Oxidation of an aldehyde gives a ____ acid.

tf.q: An aldehyde has an H on the carbonyl carbon.
tf.explain: That is why it oxidises easily.

tf.q: A ketone has an H on the carbonyl carbon.
Ketones need strong conditions to oxidise.
Oxidation of an aldehyde changes the number of carbons.
tf.explain: The acid has the same carbons.

ar.r: They have an H on the carbonyl carbon.
Oxidising them needs a C–C bond to break.

mcq.q: Strong oxidation of a ketone gives:
options: a mixture of acids with fewer carbons

num.q: How many carbons has the acid from propanal?
How many reagent systems turn C=O into CH₂ in this topic?

short.q: Why is an aldehyde oxidised more easily than a ketone?
short.solution: It has an H on the carbonyl carbon, so the C–H bond oxidises; a ketone must break a C–C bond.
